recipe.notes:
The template file must reach the engine: vllm serve --chat-template (R10). Without it vLLM only warns at startup (the warning is specific to is_original_qwen3_reranker, io_processor.py:431-447 at the v0.31.0 tag) and concatenates query and document with no frame (:677-678), so no anchor survives. The harness T0 check fails, not warns, when the engine did not load it.
template.jinja: the family's one template file, byte-identical across qwen3-reranker-0.6b/4b/8b - the stock vLLM example template with the paper's default instruction baked in (the recipe declares instruction: none; the paper's runs never vary it, and a request instruction is not read) and one trailing newline added. The extra newline is measured, not cosmetic: jinja2 environments strip a template file's final newline (keep_trailing_newline=False, the engine's own render settings), so the stock file renders the assistant suffix one newline short and the scored position lands on the wrong token (the research instrument measured last-token 'Ċ' vs 'ĊĊ' on every probe pair). The query and document read the engine's chat variables with a fallback: the /rerank route applies the template to [{role: query}, {role: document}] messages (io_processor.py:693-703), while stage 1's template check renders query/document directly; the recipe tests render both branches and stage 1's template_render_check proves the declared shape byte-equals the file.
Budget: max_tokens 8192 is the paper's MAX_SEQ_LENGTH, counted as the engine sees the whole prompt (frame + query + document); the frame's fixed overhead is 73 tokens (39-token prefix, 9-token suffix, 25 for the instruction and the query/document labels). query_max_tokens 4096 is the paper's MAX_QUERY_LENGTH, which the paper applied only on its served path; its in-process QwenOGRerank caps no query. Settle rule, read from the merged rerank client (rcp-ndcg/src/rcp_ndcg/inference/clients/rerank.py and the query_max_tokens docstring in rcp-ndcg/src/rcp_ndcg/inference/config.py): the pair fit binds on overflow (an under-budget pair is sent uncut), and the rerank client settles the shared query once per call - it ships at its declared query_max_tokens whenever the query exceeds it. Over-share queries are therefore declared divergence rows: the served span is cut at the share while the reference keeps the whole query inside its pair cut; an over-share query in an UNDER-budget pair is a declared divergence row too (reported in the non-gating table), so the pairs files of the waves keep queries well within the share (the paper's datasets do) and drop any row stage 1 goes red on.
Over-cap policy (one, family wide): the reference truncates the pair string longest_first at 8144 tokens (the paper's _process_inputs: on a single sequence a right cut, the document first, then the query tail), re-attaches the 39-token prefix and the 9-token assistant suffix - no anchor is ever dropped - and NEVER copies the client's cut, so reference.known_deviations declares over_cap_cut_differs: the harness reports over-cap rows in a non-gating table and gates under-cap rows exactly. For over-cap pairs whose query is within the share the two cuts usually keep the same content tokens (the sweep's adversarial battery measured them byte-identical for queries up to 4090 tokens); where a cut boundary lands a token apart or the query is over its share they differ, and the row is reported, never silently gated. The render comparison is character-exact on raw input text: the reference locates its cut at raw character offsets, never a decode(encode()) round trip (this checkpoint's normalizer maps non-NFC text to NFC, keeping the ids equal but not the characters).
Scores: the client declares use_activation: true and serve.pooler_config pins the same value - the converted 1-label head scores sigmoid(x.(W_yes-W_no)) (adapters.py:569-571 at the tag, float32), which equals the reference's softmax([no, yes])[yes]; both sides are probability-scale. dtype bfloat16 (the paper pipeline's DTYPE); the reference batches at 4 (the paper's 8B config) with the OOM-halving backoff the paper code carries.
Engine: the image is the unmodified vllm/vllm-openai:v0.31.0 (min_version declares the verified image; the feature floor is 0.30.1, where the conversion overrides first shipped in v0.30.1rc0); no plugin, no custom image, no extra environment. The GPU wave must check: T0 that the engine loaded template.jinja (fails, not warns), and the R29 /tokenize equality of fit's renders per shape with add_special_tokens: true (the Qwen tokenizer's post-processor adds no tokens, so both flags encode alike - the declared flag is the route's default behaviour). Reference environment: reference.in/reference.lock beside reference.py (the paper reference's pins).
